periodicity.text: The light curve is dominated by a smooth sinusoid with period 0.44548 d (Lomb-Scargle power 0.26); the adopted 1.90609 d is 4.28 x that. The true period is more likely 0.44548 d (pulsation or spots) or 0.89097 d (contact binary), and the 'eclipses' may not be eclipses.

checks: No eclipse at 28 of 123 covered epochs where the 1.90609 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.

writeup: TIC 193548084 is a newly discovered eclipsing binary star system with an orbital period of 1.906087 days. The primary eclipse causes the star to dim by 0.52 percent, while a secondary eclipse has not been detected. This candidate was identified through automated analysis with a strong signal-to-noise ratio of 83.1 and confirmed through independent pixel-level imaging techniques, which showed a centroid offset of 5.5 arcseconds from the target. Notably, this system does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs, making it a genuine discovery. The detection is further supported by the significant difference in alternating eclipse depths, a signature characteristic of the true orbital period identified through careful data analysis.
